functionalObligations.text: an investor subscribes an asset into a vault attached to a share class of a pool and receives a share token that represents a claim on the pool's assets and rises in price rather than in balance
functionalObligations.note: Live flagship: JTRSY 0x8c213ee79581ff4984583c6a801e5263418c4b86, 792,751,306.27 shares at 1.111749542989796511, that is $881.3M, read from the protocol's own public GraphQL at https://api.centrifuge.io (accessed 2026-08-04); JAAA $684.79M, ACRDX $43.45M, SPXA $3.37M, total primary share tokens $1.613B. Ix was considered and NOT emitted: the price rises because a manager posts a higher number (F4), not because any accrual rule computes one, so there is no index object. That distinction is exactly what separates Centrifuge from Ondo's USDY, where Ix is exact.

functionalObligations.text: subscription and redemption are asynchronous: a request is placed, the issuer approves a batch, shares are issued or revoked, the batch is fulfilled and only then may the investor claim
functionalObligations.note: The ERC-7540 lifecycle is pending, approved, issued or revoked, fulfilled, claimed, and the ISSUER controls approval. Ep carries the mechanism; Wq is DROPPED as a DEPARTURE from the corpus, because there is no queue, no ordering, no position and no liquidity trigger, only a batch the issuer approves. This is the exact mirror image of Maple, where Wq is right and Ep is wrong, and a decomposition that gives both symbols to both protocols loses the distinction. Sync-deposit vaults (ERC-4626 plus ERC-7540) skip the request phase for deposits only, so the asynchrony is one-sided in that configuration.

functionalObligations.text: redemption is a first-class protocol operation with its own dedicated transfer-hook regime, and it is conditional on the issuer approving the batch and setting its execution price
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus omits Rd and it should be present with a conditionality note, which is the qualification Rd needs everywhere in this category. The BatchRequestManager 0xc52Bd1Bd..3dFe77 sets the execution price for individual deposit and redemption batches SEPARATELY from the published reference price, so the price at which a holder actually exits is a second discretionary number distinct from the NAV, which is why Sv is emitted here as well as at F4. A dedicated RedemptionRestrictions hook 0xE5423eD8..17f06 exists to gate the redemption leg specifically.

functionalObligations.text: the value of every share is a single number one party posts on chain, with the freshness timestamp supplied by that same party, and no dispute window, challenge bond, deviation bound or staleness rejection anywhere in the call path
functionalObligations.note: Hub.updateSharePrice(PoolId, ShareClassId, D18 pricePoolPerShare, uint64 computedAt) at lines 314 to 323, guarded by _isManager(poolId) and nothing else, with computedAt a CALLER-SUPPLIED ARGUMENT rather than taken from the block. A pool's NAV is typically computed offchain, for example from a portfolio held with a bank or custodian, and the issuer publishes the resulting share price to the hub. Third-party oracles do not repair this: the documented Chronicle integration reads the oracle and calls THE SAME SETTER. Ex is emitted as the closest symbol and is APPROXIMATE in the corpus's own marker sense, since Ex presumes an adversarial or aggregated feed. Oa does not apply, there being no assertion and dispute game. DEPARTURE: At is DROPPED. There is no named independent attester, no assurance level, no staleness bound and no recourse, so L27 cannot be discharged at all; contrast USYC, which does have a named administrator and auditor and where At is retained but scoped to NAV rather than reserves. NAV manipulation is the primary failure mode of this design and it has no representation.

functionalObligations.text: that price is authoritative on one chain and a message-derived copy everywhere else, propagated only when somebody pays gas for it, and a per-chain manager may override the local copy with a different number
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Propagation is a separate explicit act, hub.notifySharePrice(poolId, scId, centrifugeId, msg.sender) per destination network, with no automatic propagation and no freshness check at the consuming end, so a spoke can carry a stale price indefinitely if nobody pushes. BalanceSheet.overridePricePoolPerShare additionally lets a spoke-side manager set a DIFFERENT price locally (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/centrifuge/protocol/v3.2.0/src/core/spoke/BalanceSheet.sol line 266, accessed 2026-08-04). Xm names verified messaging; it cannot say the canonical accounting lives on chain A while chain B trades a copy that may be stale or locally overridden.

functionalObligations.text: who may hold a share token is decided by a transfer hook chosen per share class from a shipped set, replaceable without redeploying the token, and the hook knows which operation it is gating
functionalObligations.note: Share tokens are ERC-20 extended with ERC-1404 and a modular hook system. Four hooks are deployed plus the option of none: FullRestrictions 0x8E680873..24a4, FreelyTransferable 0x2a9B9C14..1A61, RedemptionRestrictions 0xE5423eD8..17f06, FreezeOnly. The hook is ACTION-AWARE, distinguishing deposit requests, deposit claims, redemption requests, redemption claims, cross-chain transfers and peer-to-peer transfers, so different rules apply to different operation types, which Aw cannot carry. DOCUMENTATION DEFECT worth recording for stage 3: the docs site says FreelyTransferable requires memberlist membership for deposits and redemptions while the repository's own src/hooks/README.md says it always returns true for transfer checks (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/centrifuge/protocol/v3.2.0/src/hooks/README.md, accessed 2026-08-04); the code is authoritative and the docs page is wrong.

functionalObligations.text: eligibility carries an expiry: membership is stored as a valid-until timestamp packed into the same storage slot as the balance, so a holder ceases to be eligible with no actor doing anything
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. BaseTransferHook encodes member validity and freeze status in the hookData structure (bytes16), the first 8 bytes a uint64 memberlist valid-until timestamp and the least significant bit the freeze status, packed into the same 256-bit slot as the balance. Aw is a bit; this is a bit with a clock. Independently found in the same shape at BUIDL, whose registry attributes also carry an expiry, so this is a category-level gap rather than one protocol's quirk.

functionalObligations.text: a pool manager can freeze an address and can take shares from a wallet and move them elsewhere, and a dedicated recovery contract is deployed for it
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus omits Fz for Centrifuge and it is a clear omission. Verified in source at tag v3.2.0: transferSharesFrom at line 136 is guarded isManager(poolId), refuses to pull from an endorsed contract, and calls token.authTransferFrom on the auth-gated ShareToken; issue and revoke at lines 156 and 232 are likewise isManager. The docs name it explicitly, recover tokens from a lost wallet by forced transfer via balance sheet transferSharesFrom, alongside a per-address freeze flag in token storage. A TokenRecoverer 0x1E70530e9555711f8DF4838Ab940b97c039B4037 is deployed. Centrifuge therefore has MORE explicit freeze and forced-transfer machinery than USYC, which the corpus does credit with Fz.

functionalObligations.text: a restricted share can be wrapped into a freely transferable token that trades on top of it, while the right to mint or redeem remains behind the identity gate
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the category's cleanest instance of laundering a permissioned claim into a permissionless one. Issuers can wrap existing tokenized securities into freely transferable tokens while mint and redeem functions stay at KYC endpoints. Live: deJTRSY 0xa6233014b9b7aaa74f38fa1977ffc7a89642dc72, 18 decimals, supply 5,005,320.37 at price 1.032850, with its own hook 0xd51d8450..a2a0, plus deJAAA, deCRDX and deSPXA. The economic exposure becomes bearer and the redemption right does not: two tokens, one claim, two access regimes, and the second has no path to the obligor. RE-SITING: the corpus attaches this residue to Maple, where the measured permission level refutes it; it belongs here. Prohibition X19 (a restricted claim bridged via Xf into a representation with no destination-side Aw) does not literally fire because deRWA is a wrapper rather than a bridge, which is itself the finding: THE PROHIBITION IS DOMAIN-SPECIFIC WHERE THE HAZARD IS NOT.

functionalObligations.text: messages between chains are delivered by several independent adapters and each pool chooses which of them it trusts and how many must agree
functionalObligations.note: Xm is confirmed and materially richer than the symbol. Deployed on mainnet: Chainlink 0x39CF679E..7D955, Axelar 0x34e90423..a6484, Wormhole 0x4BE43040..706A7 and a second Wormhole adapter, aggregated behind MultiAdapter 0x35C837F0..073BE and Gateway 0x19a524D0..D3172. Each pool calls setAdapters to choose providers, a confirmation threshold setting the minimum number of adapters that must deliver a message before it is processed, and recovery adapters. RESIDUE INSIDE THE SYMBOL: Xm is a boolean, and here verification strength is A PARAMETER CHOSEN BY THE PARTY WHOSE ASSETS ARE AT RISK, so two pools on the same protocol can have materially different cross-domain security and carry the same symbol. L18 (explicit finality, domain binding, replay protection) is not separately evidenced and should be checked in stage 3.

functionalObligations.text: share tokens move between chains with the eligibility hook invoked on both the outgoing and the incoming leg
functionalObligations.note: Confirmed: limit token bridging, hook is invoked on outgoing and incoming cross-chain transfers. This means L26 (Aw plus Xf implies destination-enforced eligibility) is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION here, which is the only clean discharge of L26 in this category and is worth stating positively. Core contracts sit at identical addresses across 11 networks (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Plume, BNB, Optimism, HyperEVM, Monad, Pharos, X Layer), a correction to the corpus's and the docs' own llms.txt figure of 9.

functionalObligations.text: one immutable contract holds administrative access over every other contract in the protocol, and every escalation of privilege through it waits forty-eight hours
functionalObligations.note: The protocol is controlled by the Root contract, an immutable smart contract that holds admin (ward) access on all other contracts, mainnet 0xdc9456e7e20f15029C8231Ec433a20F404b7235E, and all privilege escalation through Root goes through a 48-hour timelock. This is the STRONGEST control plane of the five and the decomposition must not treat it as equivalent to BUIDL's single EOA or to Maple's retroactively shortenable delay; L15 is discharged here in a way it is not for Ondo, USYC or BUIDL. RESIDUE INSIDE THE PAIR: rendering this as Up plus Tg loses the actual design, which is that the AUTHORITY contract cannot be upgraded but can rewrite the permissions on everything else after two days. Immutable-but-omnipotent is a distinct shape and neither symbol names it.

functionalObligations.text: two separate guardians hold different powers on separate multisignature wallets, and only one of them can pause anything
functionalObligations.note: ProtocolGuardian 0xCEb7eD5d5B3bAD3088f6A1697738B60d829635c6 holds pause, upgrades and cross-chain powers, with every transaction verified by third-party signers from Cantina; OpsGuardian 0x055589229506Ee89645EF08ebE9B9a863486d0dE holds wiring and pool creation and has NO PAUSE AUTHORITY. Both at identical addresses on every network. Gp names the facility and cannot express that the power to halt and the power to configure are deliberately held by different parties, the same split the 06-yield lane recorded for Sky's grantors and revokers and for Huma's pauser and restarter.

functionalObligations.text: the global pause is deliberately partial: it halts all cross-chain messaging in both directions and leaves local deposits, redemptions and withdrawals running
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Verbatim: the global pause halts all cross-chain messaging, both inbound and outbound; local vault operations (deposit, redeem, withdraw) are not affected. Gp implies stopping the protocol; here the guardian can stop the nervous system while the limbs keep moving. That is arguably the right design, and the vocabulary cannot record THE SCOPE OF A PAUSE at all, so a pause that stops everything and a pause that stops messaging carry the same symbol.

functionalObligations.text: each strategist is given a merkle root encoding the exact set of calls they may make, verified per call by target contract, function selector and parameter values, and revised by replacing the root
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus does not record Au for Centrifuge at all, and the MerkleProofManager is delegated execution scope in the strongest sense the vocabulary contemplates, far more expressive than the symbol suggests. L17 (bounded scope, revocation, expiry, nonce or domain separation) is partly discharged: scope and revocation are explicit, expiry and replay separation are not evidenced. Related pool roles that Au does not reach: a hub manager can grant or revoke the hub manager role for OTHER addresses, so the top-level authority is self-propagating; a gateway manager can block outgoing messages for one pool on one destination, a pool-scoped circuit breaker; and OnOfframpManager runs a permissionless onramp against a relayer-gated offramp to pre-approved destinations.

functionalObligations.text: there is no seniority anywhere in the protocol: multiple share classes exist, they can be named and permissioned differently, and nothing allocates a loss between them
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORRECTION the corpus requires: Tr is REFUTED for V3 and DROPPED. The evidence is a code search over repo:centrifuge/protocol returning ZERO hits for waterfall, senior, junior and subordinat, and six hits for tranche, every one of them in the 2023 Code4rena audit document, a test-properties file, or a legacy env/spell/*.sol migration script, NONE IN src/ (GitHub code search, accessed 2026-08-04). The docs' junior/senior tranches phrasing describes a CONFIGURATION IDIOM: an issuer may create two share classes, whitelist them differently and price them differently. There is no loss-allocation logic, no seniority ordering, no overcollateralisation test, no interest-coverage test and no trigger that redirects anything. Subordination, where it exists in a Centrifuge pool, lives in the fund's offering documents and is expressed on chain only as the manager choosing to mark one share class down before another. The corpus's residue note about DROP and TIN describes V2 and Tinlake, not V3. CONSEQUENCE: with Tr removed, Sv becomes the ONLY symbol carrying loss allocation for this application, because the sole way a loss reaches a holder is a manager-set price.

functionalObligations.text: a defaulted underlying asset has no on-chain representation of any kind: no delinquency state, no roll rate, no write-off flag and no impairment call exist in the protocol
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the on-chain state is EMPTIER than the corpus implies. Holdings and Accounting carry valuations and journal entries; src/valuations contains exactly IdentityValuation.sol and OracleValuation.sol. A default appears only as a lower number in the next updateSharePrice call. Compare Maple, which at least has impairLoan and unrealizedLosses: Centrifuge V3 has strictly less servicing state than the corpus's phrasing, that Sv gestures at discretion but names no state, implies, because there is no state to gesture at.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know who owes them the money, and here the protocol owes them nothing: the obligor is an off-chain fund and Centrifuge is infrastructure
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. For the flagship share class the issuer is Anemoy Capital SPC Limited, a British Virgin Islands segregated portfolio company regulated by the BVI Financial Services Commission; the protocol is a set of contracts with no claim against it. The entity details beyond BVI regulation (Anemoy Asset Management as investment manager, Janus Henderson as sub-investment manager) rest on web-search consensus and are marked UNCONFIRMED at a primary source. No element names an obligor. The structural point that distinguishes Centrifuge from the other four: the obligor is DIFFERENT PER SHARE CLASS on the same protocol, since five issuers use it, so a decomposition of the protocol is not a decomposition of any holder's claim, and the vocabulary has no way to mark that separation.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know whether the chain is the register, and here the token is prima facie evidence of ownership under BVI law in the same way a share certificate would be
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the third of three distinct legal devices in this category. Prima facie evidence is precisely NOT the register: a share certificate is rebuttable evidence of an entry in a book kept elsewhere. So all three fund-wrapped instruments place the chain BELOW an off-chain register, by three different routes, BUIDL through a US transfer agent's books and records, USYC through a fund administrator's share registry and an explicit digital-twin metaphor, and JTRSY through the BVI law of share certificates. The vocabulary has ONE WORD, none, for three distinct legal relationships, AND THE DIFFERENCES DETERMINE WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE CHAIN AND THE BOOK DISAGREE: under BUIDL's device the book simply wins and the transfer is not a redemption; under USYC's the book is updated to follow; under Anemoy's the holder must go to a BVI court and rebut.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know whether their claim survives the issuer's insolvency, and here a bankruptcy-remote structure is asserted by the issuer and no security trustee is named anywhere
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Anemoy's own page states the fund is a registered and regulated fund approved by the BVI Financial Services Commission with a bankruptcy remote SPV structure. CORRECTION: the corpus's security trustee holding the assets for tokenholders' benefit is NOT EVIDENCED and is marked UNKNOWN; no security trustee is named in anything fetched and no offering document is public. What IS nameable in fact and not in vocabulary is the SPC form itself: a segregated portfolio company statutorily ring-fences each portfolio's assets from the others' liabilities, which is a legal firewall between claim classes that looks superficially like Im (isolated market) but is created by BVI statute rather than by contract deployment and survives insolvency, which Im does not claim to do. Im is NOT emitted for that reason: it would attribute to a deployment a property that only a statute confers.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know what the reserve holds and who custodies it, and here the fund discloses the roles and names none of the parties
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The fund states that it works with an independent prime broker, custodian, tokenization and issuance, and fund admin service providers. UNKNOWN: the names of the administrator, custodian, prime broker and auditor; the page discloses roles WITHOUT ENTITIES. Nothing on chain records what the portfolio holds either: Holdings and Accounting carry valuations, not instruments, and there is no reserve report of any kind. At is not emitted (see F4), so on this construction the protocol asserts a price and attests nothing.

functionalObligations.text: the holder must know who may change what the money is invested in, and here nothing on chain records who selected an asset or on what criteria
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirmed unnameable, and the boundary must be stated because Centrifuge is the case that most tempts a forced fit. The MerkleProofManager emitted at F15 constrains WHAT CALLS A STRATEGIST MAY MAKE, which is an execution-scope constraint, not a credit criterion; Au therefore bounds the mechanics of allocation while saying nothing about its merits. The vocabulary has no way to distinguish a pool whose assets were chosen by a rated manager from one whose assets were chosen arbitrarily. Fifth of five products in this category with unconstrained, invisible investment discretion, and the fifth independent confirmation in this lane of the delegated allocation mandate the 06-yield and 03-CDP lanes identified as a missing level above the element.
